title: World Rugby FPRC Decision Ollie Sapsford
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Sapsford Player’s Ollie
forename(s)
Player’s Union Rugby Australia
Match Australia A v Japan XV
Competition - Match Date 18 October 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence 9.11 Players must not do anything that is
reckless or dangerous to others including
leading with the elbow or forearm, or
jumping into, or over, a tackler.
Finding of Committee Foul Play admitted
Foul play determined? Foul play determined.
Red card upheld? Red Card upheld.
Summary of Sanction Three (3) week suspension. Should the Player apply for and successfully complete the Coaching
Intervention Programme (if applicable) the suspension may be reduced to (2) weeks.
Matches/tournaments Three (3) matches for :
included in sanction
Match 1 ACT Brumbies v HKCR - 8 November 2025
Match 2 ACT Brumbies v Western Force - 30 January 2026
Match 3 ACT Brumbies v Waratahs - 4 February 2026
The Player will be free to play in Match 3 if he applies for and completes the Coaching
Intervention Programme, if applicable.
REASONS FOR DECISION
Evidence
1. The FPRC received and considered the following material:
a. video clip of the incident;
b. five (5) Match Official Reports from the Referee, Assistant Referees, TMO and FPRO;
c. victim player’s (Japan 14) statement and medical report;
d. the Player’s submission. There Player accepted foul play but did not accept that the Red Card threshold was
met.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 2

Decision
2. The FPRC upheld the Red Card applying the Head Contact Process (2023):
a. head contact – Yes. The Player’s right shoulder made contact with Japan #14’s neck and/or head;
b. foul play – Yes. The Player’s actions were reckless. He was upright and he admitted he got his positioning
wrong;
c. degree of danger – High. The Player was dynamic. There was high force (Japan #14 described “intense
contact”); and
d. mitigation – None. The Player had clear line of sight. He did not make an attempt to change his height. There
was no significant drop or movement from Japan #14.
Sanction
3. The FPRC applied the mandatory mid-range entry point of 6 weeks due to the head contact. There was no injury
and the victim player played on. There was no basis for moving to top end.
4. Based on the Player’s clean record and experience the FPRC applied full mitigation 3 weeks (reducing sanction to
3 weeks). The player is eligible for the Coaching Intervention Programme, if applicable. If the Player applies and
completes the programme, the suspension may be reduced to two (2) weeks.
Note:
In the FPRC’s view, the appliable foul play for this incident should be Law 9.13 – Dangerous Tackling instead of Law 9.11.
Whilst there are no provisions under the Expedited Off-Field Sanctioning process which would permit the FPRC to amend
the appliable foul play, the FPRC notes the mandatory mid-range entry point for both 9.11 and 9.13 is the same.
Foul Play Review Ofisa Tonu’u (NZ)
Committee Members
Valeriu Toma (ROM)
Signature Date 19 October 2025
Chair
Wang Shao-Ing
